title: Meta Muse and Instinct Concierge can now make phone calls for you
key_facts: Instinct founder Noah Shinn announced Instinct Concierge on 16 Sep 2026; it lets the company's AI assistant place phone calls to businesses, in early access for some users.
Examples given: booking a restaurant without online reservations, getting on a dentist's cancellation list, sorting a cable bill.
Instinct raised $250 million in August at a $2.5 billion valuation and announced a $1 billion Series C on 28 Sep 2026 at a $10 billion valuation, with Sequoia, Benchmark and Coatue.
Meta has reportedly been testing an outbound-calling feature letting some Muse users ask the agent to call US businesses; it remains in limited testing.
Muse launched 8 Sep 2026, is available in the US and Canada, has a free tier and reported paid plans at $20 and $100 a month; no separate price announced for calling.

Instinct's terms warn that agent actions may contain errors and may not be reversible; its privacy policy says the assistant can access messages, emails, credentials and payment information when permitted.
Meta says Muse runs in a dedicated secure virtual machine, cannot see stored passwords or payment methods, asks approval before sensitive actions and keeps an audit trail.
quote_evidence: Instinct can now place phone calls to businesses for some early-access users, while Meta is testing a similar capability with Muse.
Meta has reportedly been testing an outbound-calling capability that lets some Muse users ask the agent to call U.S. businesses.
The company says its services can produce incorrect or incomplete information. It also warns that actions may contain errors and may not always be reversible.
why_it_matters_hint: Agents are moving from typing to speaking on users' behalf, which widens convenience and the privacy and liability questions.
event_date: Instinct Concierge 16 Sep 2026; Muse calling test undated, reported as ongoing
notes: Column piece; the Muse calling test is attributed to unnamed reports. The Instinct announcement is more than two weeks old, so the item is a follow-up rather than new news.
